name: 3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Synthase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for HMG-CoA Synthase Deficiency

criteria.description: Episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia triggered by fasting or illness
Elevated plasma ammonia and transaminases with low or absent ketone bodies during metabolic crisis
Identification of pathogenic variants in the HMGCS2 gene
Increased dicarboxylic acids and 4-hydroxy-6-methyl-2-pyrone in urine during crisis
Reduced HMG-CoA synthase enzyme activity in liver or fibroblasts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia with biochemical abnormalities plus confirmation by genetic testing or enzyme assay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed during acute metabolic crises triggered by fasting or illness.

laboratory: Urine organic acid profile showing increased dicarboxylic acids and 4-hydroxy-6-methyl-2-pyrone
imaging: Brain MRI may show reversible changes consistent with metabolic encephalopathy during crises
other: Reduced HMG-CoA synthase enzyme activity in liver biopsy or cultured fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Muscle weakness and rhabdomyolysis more prominent

redFlags: Recurrent hypoketotic hypoglycemia with metabolic encephalopathy
Severe metabolic crisis triggered by fasting or illness
Elevated plasma ammonia without liver failure
references: Matern D, et al. Disorders of ketone body metabolism. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
Roe CR, et al. HMG-CoA synthase deficiency: a new disorder of ketogenesis. J Clin Invest. 1993;91(4):1283-1288.
